verdict.rationale: turbopuffer documents generally available sharding that scales a single namespace up to 256TB. Its architecture separates object-storage state from NVMe/memory-cached compute, which it says scales queries to petabyte scale. This directly addresses scaling beyond one node, though the evidence is mostly roadmap and summary claims. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of how sharding is configured and operated, independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-node scaling behavior.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can scale beyond one node with sharding or distributed deployment

citations.quote: Sharding is generally available: scale a single namespace up to 256TB
Using only object storage for state and NVMe SSD with memory cache for compute, turbopuffer scales low-latency queries to petabyte scale.
Namespace pinning provisions reserved compute for a namespace to provide predictable cost and performance for large namespaces with sustained query volume
